_about: Splits the 28 concept tags into four kinds. Applied to tag.facet by scripts/migrate.js.

_tests.irreducible: Cannot be decomposed into other concepts in the catalogue.
_tests.widespread: Many unrelated domains point at it.
_tests.importable: You can name the concrete thing you would import.
_tests.implemented: Something implements it. A concept is a thing you can be sent away to build; if nothing implements it, it is a property of work rather than a way of doing any, and it belongs on an axis.

_kinds.block: Passes all three tests. Substrate — everything else is built out of these.
_kinds.representation: A format for holding structure, not a way of making it. A block makes; a representation stores.
_kinds.category: Fails the importable test. A bag containing blocks that were never named separately.
_kinds.deployment: Where or how something runs. Not a concept at all — both of these are carried by the axis layer now, and their tag rows are what it is classified from.

_note: The importable test is the one that does the work. `sim` is used in 21 of 23 domains — wider than anything but `rand` — and still fails, because there is no simulator you can import. That is why it became a dumping ground. The fourth test is the one that took longest to state and is the easiest to check: `shader` and `kit` are the only two concepts here with no algorithm rows, which is what an axis looks like from the algorithm layer.

_contains._about: Blocks hiding inside each category that the catalogue never named separately. These are candidates for the algorithms layer, not records that exist yet.

_contested: dsp — called a block, but digital signal processing is really a category containing Karplus–Strong, FM, granular and modal synthesis. Those are the actual blocks. Same shape as `sim`, just smaller, so it may belong with the categories.
ero — three methods (hydraulic, thermal, aeolian) under one label. A small category rather than a block, on the same argument as `dsp`.
part — BSP, quadtrees and k-d trees are data structures, which argues representation. But recursive subdivision is an operation, which argues block. Filed as representation; could go either way.

gram — filed as a category because it spans CGA, Tracery and graph grammars, yet `lsys` is separately a block. That is deliberate: `gram` is the umbrella, `lsys` is one named formalism inside it. It does mean the two overlap.

graph — 'graph algorithms' is arguably a category too (MST, shortest path, max-flow, matching are separate blocks). Kept as a block because the underlying structure is one thing and the algorithms over it are tightly related.
tile — spans periodic tilings, aperiodic tilings, wallpaper groups and phyllotaxis. Defensible as a category.
